body: Should maybe be `image_resource_format.h` to match the convention elsewhere, even though the original file is `ImageLoader`. I guess this one is a bit of a special case.
I love seeing this kind of change that shows that the efforts _are_ meaningful :D

That's a good example of why I'm not so fond of having two different names for the same enum (though here it's not even the same enum as we don't have `using enum`). The `.cpp` file still uses `ResourceFormatLoader::CacheMode` so the definition and declaration differ.

I'm not saying that _not_ having the alias would be better though. It reduces the diff quite a bit.

Should this be `ResourceLoaderEnums` to match the convention used elsewhere?

Or can we find a better common name that could also fit `ResourceUID::ID` from #117516?

Oh I just forgot to update the cpp.
But yeah if I didn't do the `using` tricks, the diff would have another ~200 files with just name changes...
Regarding it being the same enum, it functionally is because of all the `static constexpr` but that's only true as long as the enum doesn't change. I'd much rather have `using enum` too.
